analysis.evidence: In עַם אֶחָד, “one people,” the masculine singular אֶחָד agrees with עַם. The parallel phrase וְשָׂפָה אַחַת לְכֻלָּם, “and one language for them all,” identifies the speakers as a single community.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עַם אֶחָד describes the builders collectively as “one people.” The parallel phrase וְשָׂפָה אַחַת לְכֻלָּם, “and one language for them all,” ties their unity to the language they share.
analysis.morphology: The cardinal numeral follows עַם and agrees with it in the masculine singular absolute. It has no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: one and the same; made one, united

analysis.evidence: וְשָׂפָה אַחַת לְכֻלָּם means ‘and one language for them all.’ It parallels עַם אֶחָד ‘one people’ and identifies the language they all share.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ ‘and’ prefixes a feminine singular absolute common noun. The numeral אַחַת ‘one’ agrees with it in gender.

analysis.evidence: In וְשָׂפָה אַחַת לְכֻלָּם, לְכֻלָּם means “for all of them,” so אַחַת describes the language they all share.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral agreeing with שָׂפָה, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: one and the same; made one, united

analysis.evidence: In וְשָׂפָה אַחַת לְכֻלָּם, the people just called עַם אֶחָד share one language. כֹּל includes the entire group.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ precedes the masculine singular construct noun כֹּל. The third-person masculine plural suffix refers to the people.

analysis.evidence: In וְזֶה הַחִלָּם לַעֲשׂוֹת, the suffix refers to the people, and לַעֲשׂוֹת supplies the action they have begun: ‘This is what they have begun to do.’
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with a third-person masculine plural suffix that supplies its subject, ‘they’. The initial הַ is part of the Hiphil form.

analysis.evidence: וְזֶה הַחִלָּם לַעֲשׂוֹת means “and this is what they have begun to do.” זֶה points to the building work already under way.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition לַ marks the Qal infinitive construct עֲשׂוֹת as the complement of הַחִלָּם.

draft.definition: לֹא negates a statement, here a statement about the future.
draft.evidence: Gen.9.15 uses לֹא before יִהְיֶה in the promise that the waters will never again become a flood to destroy all flesh. Gen.9.11 uses the same construction in the same promise.

analysis.evidence: לֹא negates the following verb יִבָּצֵר, “will be beyond reach.” The clause predicts that nothing they plan to do will be beyond their reach.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew negative particle with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Denies that a future event will occur.

analysis.evidence: מֵהֶם identifies whose reach is in view. With לֹא negating the verb and כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יָזְמוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת as its subject, the clause means “nothing they plan to do will be beyond their reach.”
analysis.morphology: Niphal imperfect, third person masculine singular, with כֹּל as its subject.

analysis.evidence: כֹּל stands on its own as the head of כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יָזְמוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת, “everything they plan to do.” With לֹא יִבָּצֵר מֵהֶם, the clause means “nothing they plan to do will be beyond their reach.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
Indeclinable relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יָזְמוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת, “whatever they plan to do,” לַעֲשׂוֹת gives the action they intend. The clause concerns what the people can accomplish together and gives no indication that they intend harm.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine plural. The initial י and final וּ mark the inflection. The subject is the people acting together.
